en: WHAT THIS IS
A runtime overclock for Symbian 9.2 phones
built on the TI OMAP 2420: Nokia N95 8GB
and Nokia E90. It changes the DPLL
multiplier and the clock dividers while the
phone is running.
SAFETY - READ THIS FIRST
Nothing is ever written to flash. Every
change lives in registers only, so a reboot
always returns the phone to its stock
330 MHz. The worst outcome of a bad setting
is an immediate reboot, and you lose only
what was unsaved.
HOW TO USE IT
1. MULT sets the DPLL multiplier. The
header shows what the new setting gives
before you apply anything.
2. APPLY SETTING only arms the change.
3. CONFIRM performs it, stepping one
multiplier at a time.
4. RESTORE STOCK puts the multiplier back.
Stock is 86, that is 330 MHz. Both phones
reach about 500 MHz without a voltage
change, which is the silicon limit.
THE BUS MATTERS MORE THAN THE CORE
In 3D this chip is limited by memory, not by
the CPU. On the E90 raising the bus alone
took 16.3 to 24.6 fps with the core left
untouched. BUSDIV sets the bus divider, and
a smaller divider means a faster bus.
BUS GUARD
Returning the bus from a lowered state back
to stock rebooted the phone four times out
of four. The guard therefore refuses to
raise the bus and is ON by default. Turn it
off only if you accept a likely reboot.
THE TESTS
TEST cpu/alu measures the core and TEST mem
bandwidth measures the bus. The two must
move independently: that is how you tell a
real change from a reported one. TEST sdram
integrity catches silent memory corruption,
so run it after any bus change.
TEST cache currently does far more
arithmetic per byte than the memory test, so
its number reflects the ALU and cannot be
compared with the memory result.
IF THE PHONE REBOOTS
Nothing is damaged. Switch it on and it
comes up at stock clocks. Step back one
multiplier and try again.
